Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: PoC Deployment Mode — Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private VPC

Hi Sam / Priya,

Thanks again for your time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery: Acme is prioritizing throughput for high-concurrency inference (customer chat use case), strict data isolation for PII, and predictable unit economics. You mentioned compliance requirements that might push you toward Dedicated or Private VPC.

Next steps I outlined on the call:
- Confirm preferred deployment mode (Hosted API initial eval vs Dedicated reserved capacity vs Private VPC/on-prem)
- Agree on PoC success criteria (latency percentile, tokens/sec, monthly cost target, data residency)
- Identify stakeholders we should include for a technical kickoff (SRE, Security, Procurement)
- Draft a 3-week PoC/trial plan to validate capacity and integration effort

Can you confirm which deployment mode you want us to align the PoC to? I'm happy to propose two parallel tracks (short Hosted pilot + Dedicated carryover) if you'd like to accelerate validation while contracts finalize.

I'll prepare a short SOW draft and security questionnaire for your team — attaching the draft SOW and our security QA in the follow-up.

Thanks,
Ben

Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: PoC Deployment Mode — Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private VPC

Ben — thanks for the recap and the clear next steps.

Short answer on deployment mode: Dedicated reserved capacity is our preferred target. Primary reasons:
- Data isolation and tenant controls for PII are non-negotiable for our security team
- Predictable latency at scale (we expect sustained concurrency during peak periods)
- Budgeting prefers a committed model if the performance/price tradeoff checks out

That said, we are open to a very short Hosted pilot (1 week) to validate integration and basic latency before we spin up Dedicated, assuming we can port the workload without rewrite.

Success criteria I want to see in the PoC:
1) 95th percentile latency <= 350ms for our 1k concurrent sessions benchmark
2) End-to-end request throughput >= 5k tokens/sec sustained (30-minute window)
3) No PII persistence outside our VPC (if Dedicated) and clear KMS usage
4) Integration with our existing SSO and audit logging (or a documented plan to achieve it)
5) Monthly cost projection within 15% of current forecast (we'll provide a baseline)

Stakeholders: Priya (Security), myself (AI infra), plus Procurement (Contracts) — cc'd. Please include SRE/infra contact and a technical lead from Redwood for the Dedicated sizing conversation.

Also please share a proposed timeline and the SOW so Procurement can start reviewing.

Sam
Sam Johnson
Head of AI Infrastructure, Acme Corp

Thanks Sam — that feedback is perfect. Based on your priorities, here's a proposed PoC/trial plan (3-week focused engagement) and what we will deliver: 

PoC objective: Validate Dedicated reserved capacity performance and integration while optionally running a 1-week Hosted pilot to accelerate app-level validation.

Week 0 (prep - 3 business days):
- Kickoff with stakeholders (SRE, Security, Procurement) — schedule 60m technical kickoff
- Exchange access: test dataset, baseline perf numbers, SSO test accounts, procurement contacts
- Redwood provides SOW draft and security QA (attached)

Week 1 (optional Hosted pilot - 5 business days):
- Short Hosted trial to validate integration and basic latency with a small reserved token budget
- Goal: validate request/response integration, logging, and end-to-end tracing

Week 2 (Dedicated sizing & deployment):
- Redwood proposes Dedicated GPU pool sizing based on telemetry from pilot and your baseline
- Dedicated environment deployed in your chosen region, KMS integration for keys
- Ramp traffic to reach target concurrency in staged fashion

Week 3 (Validation & Handoff):
- Run defined benchmarks (95p latency, tokens/sec) and run customer workload for 30-minute sustained window
- Collect logs, create regression report, and produce final cost projection
- Final review with SRE/Security and Procurement; recommended next steps for go-live

Success criteria (to be confirmed with your team):
- 95th percentile latency <= 350ms under target load
- Sustained throughput >= 5k tokens/sec for a 30-minute window
- No unauthorized PII persistence; KMS verified for key management
- SSO & audit logging integrated or a documented remediation plan
- Cost projection within 15% of your baseline

Stakeholders we will include from Redwood:
- Marissa Cole (Solutions Engineer) — technical lead for Dedicated sizing & benchmarks
- Jordan Blake (Customer Success) — PoC orchestration and success metrics
- Myself (Ben) — commercial/project lead

Please review and confirm: (A) whether you want us to run the optional Hosted week 1 pilot, and (B) available dates for the kickoff next week. If Procurement wants to start reviewing, I'll attach a short SOW and the security QA to this thread.

Regards,
Ben

Thanks Ben & Sam — this plan looks good. A few clarifications from Security & Procurement: 

1) We agree Dedicated is the end goal. However, Procurement prefers to see a short Hosted pilot (1 week) first so internal teams can validate integration before committing budget for Dedicated. That aligns with Sam's note.

2) Security: we'll need the KMS plan and confirmation that the Dedicated deployment will not persist PII outside Acme's environment. Please confirm the KMS integration approach and whether Redwood will provide a key rotation schedule.

3) Procurement: attached is our standard procurement timeline. If Redwood can provide a pricing estimate for the 3-week PoC + projected monthly price for Dedicated (by GPU profile), Procurement can start an internal approval. We also need the SOW and redlines turned around within 5 business days.

I've attached the security questionnaire and procurement timeline worksheets. We'll aim to do kickoff the week of Jul 26 — can Marissa or Jordan confirm availability for a 60m technical kickoff that week?

Thanks,
Priya Shah
Senior Director, Security Engineering
Acme Corp
